einzeiler: Chris Harris joins to discuss his new book and fantasy football draft strategies.
kurzfassung: Podcast host Chris Harris discusses his upcoming football-themed novel "Pound Foolish" and reflects on the moral complexities of following professional football. The conversation shifts to fantasy football draft strategies, where Harris and the host debate running back valuation, wide receiver depth, and player evaluation pitfalls. They also analyze several notable player battles, team backfields, and wide receiver prospects ahead of the new season.
stichpunkte: Chris Harris discusses his new football-themed novel "Pound Foolish" and his upcoming reading tour.
The hosts reflect on the moral compromises and emotional toll of engaging with professional football.
Harris emphasizes that running backs remain the most scarce commodity in fantasy football drafts.
The wide receiver position is described as extremely deep and flat beyond a few elite options.
Harris and the host discuss overreliance on combine forty times, specifically using Amari Hampton as an example.
The conversation covers college production profiles, including the evaluation of Jenarium Price.
Breakdown of team backfield situations including New England and Pittsburgh.
Analysis of wide receiver matchups like Luther Burden versus Rome Odunze and Brian Thomas versus Parker Washington.

Notable Wide Receiver Battles and Final Thoughts

clips.text: The hosts discuss the physical sacrifices, constant roster turnover, and behavioral issues players endure.

clips.hook: The numbers game of positional scarcity
clips.text: The conversation shifts to strong convictions in fantasy football analysis and how player valuation differs from consensus views.

clips.hook: Sending modern wide receivers back to 1970
clips.text: Saquon Barkley's historical rushing production is used to argue that elite players remain valuable despite sharing touches.
